2026-12-03.title: First Thursday of Annunciation · St Francis Xavier
2026-12-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; verify with the 2026–27 calendar)
readings: There is no other God besides me
2026-12-03.alt: Weekday readings: 1 Timothy 4:11–16 (Be an example in holiness); Matthew 24:45–51 (Be vigilant).
2026-12-03.verse: And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.”
theo: St Francis Xavier (1506–1552), Jesuit companion of St Ignatius, arrived in Goa in 1542 and spent years among the fishing communities of the southern coast of India, including Travancore, teaching the catechism and baptising thousands. He went on to Malacca and Japan and died on the island of Sancian, within sight of China. His body rests in Goa. The Church honours him as patron of the missions.

The readings for his feast speak of mission: God's own people, holy to the Lord (Deuteronomy); the call to “all the ends of the earth” to turn and be saved (Isaiah); the apostle who is “poor, yet making many rich” (2 Corinthians); and the Twelve sent two by two with nothing but a staff (Mark). In this season of announcements, Xavier reminds us that the Good News must be announced to everyone.
outline: Ask: who brought the Gospel to the fishing villages of our coast?
Point 1 · Turn to me, all the ends of the earth
God's salvation is for every nation.
Point 2 · Poor, yet making many rich
Xavier gave up everything to give Christ.
Mission depends on God, not on resources.
live: Pray for Kerala missionaries serving in North India, Africa and elsewhere.
Let your words and conduct today announce Christ.
saints: Patron of missions; laboured in Goa, along the southern Indian coast, Malacca and Japan; body venerated in Goa.
2026-12-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, you sent St Francis Xavier to bring your Gospel to our land and to the East. Give us his zeal, his poverty and his love, and send labourers into your harvest. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana we are sent: the dismissal is a mission. Like the Twelve, we leave the church carrying Christ to the ends of our own small worlds.

quick: St Francis Xavier carried the Gospel along India's southern coast.
God's salvation is for all the ends of the earth.
Mission depends on God's power, not on resources.
2026-12-03.question: Whom am I called to bring the Good News to?

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends two by two to tell people about God. St Francis Xavier came all the way to India to tell people about Jesus. We can tell others about Jesus too.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries, especially priests and sisters from Kerala working far away.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family help someone know Jesus this week?”

pm.open: Lord of the harvest, you sent your apostles to the ends of the earth and brought St Francis Xavier to our shores. Send your Spirit upon us as we gather, and make us missionaries of your love. Amen.
share: Paul says the apostles were poor yet made many rich (2 Corinthians 6:10). What riches of faith did missionaries bring to my family?
Jesus sent the Twelve with nothing (Mark 6:8). What do I rely on more than God?
Where is my mission field this week?
pm.resp: Lord, send us to proclaim your love.
interc: For missionaries throughout the world, especially those from our Church, that they may be strengthened.
For the people of the coastal regions of India, who received the faith through St Francis Xavier.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life in our families.
For Christians working abroad, that they may be witnesses of Christ in their workplaces.
For those who have never heard the Gospel, that they may come to know Christ.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you made St Francis Xavier a herald of the Gospel in our land. Through his prayers, give us his zeal and his joy, and make our lives a proclamation of your love. Amen.

illus: A nurse from Kerala working in a hospital in the Gulf was asked by a dying patient why she was always so gentle. She said simply: “Because Jesus is gentle with me.” That night the patient asked her to pray for him. Mission happens wherever a Christian lives the Gospel.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we celebrate St Francis Xavier, the great missionary who preached on the coasts of South India, including Travancore, nearly five centuries ago. Many of our Latin and Syro-Malabar brothers and sisters along the coast trace their faith to his work.

The readings speak of mission. Isaiah calls: turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth (Isaiah 45:22). God's salvation is not for one nation but for all. Francis took this literally: he travelled from Spain to India, Malacca, the Moluccas and Japan, and died within sight of China.

St Paul describes the life of a true apostle: in hardships, calamities, sleepless nights, hunger; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:4–10). This was Francis's life. He slept little, ate little, and gave everything; yet he was full of joy.

In the Gospel Jesus sends out the Twelve with nothing but a staff: no bread, no bag, no money (Mark 6:8). They were to depend on God and on the hospitality of those who received them. And they went out, preaching repentance, casting out demons and healing the sick.

Mission is not only for priests and sisters. Every baptised person is sent. You are sent to your family, your workplace, your school, your neighbourhood. Many of us are in mission territory without knowing it: offices in the Gulf, campuses in Bengaluru, hospitals in Europe.

How do we bring Christ? Francis taught the catechism with simple songs, cared for the sick, and above all loved people. We too can witness by honesty, kindness, prayer before meals in public, and a willingness to share our faith when someone asks.

Let us pray for missionaries today, especially for priests and sisters from our own Church serving in North India, Africa and elsewhere. And let us ask St Francis Xavier to make each of us a missionary where we live. Amen.
kids: Children, St Francis Xavier taught children prayers with songs. Sing a prayer song today and teach it to a friend!

intro: St Francis Xavier, apostle of the southern coast of India and patron of missions.

points.h: A people holy to the Lord
sub: God declares Israel his treasured people.
The baptised are called to holiness and mission.
q: Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people, as he promised you, and to keep his commandments.
He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal call to holiness.

points.h: Turn to me and be saved
sub: Salvation is offered to all the ends of the earth.
Xavier went to the farthest ends he could reach.
q: Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.”

sub: The Servant is a light to the nations.
q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent.
points.apply: Share your faith with one person this week.

concl: Xavier was poor, yet made many rich.
The Gospel must be announced to all.
2026-12-03.resolve: Support a mission diocese or missionary this season.
